channel.title: The Clanton Advertiser - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Clanton Advertiser (clantonadvertiser.com)

item.title: Strawberry Queens recognized at Thorsby City Council Meeting
item.description: Thorsby council honors 2025 Strawberry Queens as their reign nears its end. Other items discussed at the Feb. 3 Thorsby City Council meeting.

item.title: Amber Skidmore’s The Pam Family educates children on medicine
item.description: Addictions coach Amber Skidmore turns a family medicine scare into “The Pam Family,” a children’s book using playful characters to teach kids medication types and safety.

item.title: Postseason berths on the line in area basketball tournaments
item.description: All 14 Chilton County area basketball teams face win-or-go-home road tests in area tournaments Feb. 5-11, needing at least one victory to keep postseason hopes alive.

item.title: CCHS soccer hits pitch for new season
item.description: CCHS soccer opens 2026 with head coach Brandon Gurganus leading both varsity teams, a mix of veterans and youth and a first in-county match as the Tigers pursue their first playoff berth and girls area win.

item.title: Sunshine Restorations opens near Interstate 65
item.description: Sunshine Restorations, a fire, mold and water damage company specializing in crawl spaces, has opened near Interstate 65 in Clanton, offering cleanup and smoky odor removal for homes.

item.title: Chilton queen groups sew Pillows for a Cure
item.description: Six Chilton County queen groups sewed 24 pillowcases for the 11th annual Pillow Fight for a Cure, supporting cancer patients at Birmingham's Joe Lee Griffin Hope Lodge.

item.title: Elliot-Elrod scores another computer grant for Jemison
item.description: Jemison High’s Brooke Elliot-Elrod secures a new $10,000 Project Lead The Way grant through Lockheed Martin for mobile equipment in her AP computer science and cybersecurity classes.

item.title: Leonard discusses loyalty amongst reclassification in Alabama high school football
item.description: Isabella coach Tate Leonard reflects on AHSAA’s landmark public-private football split, widespread recruiting and fading loyalty in Alabama high school programs.

item.title: Sweet donation made to Crumpton, Alabama Lions Sight by Swedish Queens
item.description: Swedish Queens donate dozens of glasses to support Miss Iron City Teen Cambree Crumpton’s Alabama Lions Sight platform; more donations accepted in downtown Clanton.

item.title: Hamilton nearing 4,000 career points after surpassing varsity milestone
item.description: Chilton Christian Academy senior guard Cayman Hamilton tops 2,000 varsity points and nears 4,000 for his career while rewriting school records before heading to UAB to study medicine.
